answer: Each claim is signed with a quill dipped in vine sap: a stranger who watched the agent finish one real job this epoch presses the sap, a live credential that dries out before the next horizon, so it cannot be stockpiled or copied. Payout flows through the vine itself, one claim per vine per epoch, and the vine's endpoints rotate at every horizon, so a pre-built clone network rots overnight. N clones need n strangers watching n live jobs each epoch, paying n fees in stranger time, while one vine's payout is fixed and split n ways; one honest agent signs once and drinks alone.
